body: Seems like we have max 4 pump threads in the editor, so this might be an issue for Web and low-end hardware. Maybe we can spawn an extra thread instead of crashing (at least if total number of threads is low), it's not efficient, but should work.

This logic is wrong. Calling thread isn't necessarily the main thread. I'll just remove it since it isn't needed for the fix. 

But I do think we should improve this logic.

That's a good idea. We could just warn the user that the setting is too long and then spawn a new thread. 

I'll check and see if there are any issues with adding threads to the WTP at run time. Right now we only ever create threads when it is initialized as far as I can tell
Nevermind, this is needed. We will deadlock if we call a pump task from the calling thread since it means the calling thread will never finish the task that lead to the creation of the pump task

Might be useful to communicate how we're dealing with the situation:

```suggestion
			print_verbose(vformat("A greater number of dedicated threads were requested (%i) than threads available (%i). Please increase the number of available worker task threads. Recovering this session by spawning more worker task threads.", pump_task_count, thread_count));
```

I don't think `FixedVector` can work, because `threads` needs to have a dynamic size according to `WorkerThreadPool::init`.

The regular 'safe' resize option would be to change `threads` to hold `ThreadData *` instead of `ThreadData`. On indexed access, this would mean an additional dereference. I don't think it will lead to noticeable regressions, but I can't' guarantee it.

The `reserve` trick also seems OK for me. It would hold until we get more pump threads, which kinda seems like a ticking time bomb, but I'm also not sure we'll have this system forever anyway. I don't fully understand pump tasks yet but my impression so far has been sceptical.
